original_value: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are deployed in sensitive applications, such as in military and asset monitoring. In these applications, it is important to ensure good source location privacy. This is owing to the open nature of WSNs and the easiness of an adversary to eavesdrop on sensor communication and back trace the location of the source node. This paper proposes a scheme to preserve the source location privacy based on random routing techniques. To achieve high privacy, packets are randomly routed from the source to the sink node through strategically positioned mediate or diversion nodes. The random selection of mediate or diversion nodes is location-based. Depending on the location of the source node, packets are forwarded through different regions of the network. The proposed scheme guarantees that successive packets are routed through very different routing paths and adversaries find it confusing to back trace them to the source node location. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively confuses the adversary and provides higher source location privacy to outperform other routing-based source location privacy schemes.

result.paraphrase: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are used in sensitive settings such as military operations and asset monitoring, where protecting source location privacy is crucial. Because WSNs are open by nature, an adversary can easily eavesdrop on sensor communications and trace packets back to the source node. This paper presents a source location privacy scheme based on random routing techniques. To provide strong privacy, packets are sent randomly from the source to the sink through strategically placed mediate or diversion nodes. The choice of mediate or diversion nodes is based on location, so packets are routed through different regions of the network depending on where the source node is. The scheme ensures that successive packets follow very different paths, making it difficult for adversaries to trace them back to the source node’s location. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme effectively confuses adversaries and offers higher source location privacy than other routing-based source location privacy schemes.
